input.root_cause:
The AuditTrail plugin's config (plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml) was changed to "debug: true" at about 06:17:01, after startup (startup had loaded debug=false; a reload at 06:17:02 logged debug=true). With debug on, AuditTrail wrote every packet as a TRACE line into plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-N.log at roughly 1.5 MB/s, filling the 443 MB volume from 23 MB to about 167 MB within about two minutes. I did not identify who or what made the config change.</root_cause>
<parameter name="actions">Checked status (TPS 20, disk 23 MB of 443 MB). Observed disk jump from 23 MB to 98 MB in 45 s. Ran fs_du, which pointed to plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log and trace-1.log. Read plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml (debug: true, retention-days: 30). Overwrote config.yml with "debug: false / retention-days: 30" (the only change: debug flag). Trace growth continued, so I ran console command "audittrail" (help listing shows /audittrail reload) and then "/audittrail reload"; the log confirmed "config reloaded (debug=false)" at 06:17:38. Verified trace files stopped growing (143.6 MB total, stable across several checks) and disk held at 167 MB (38%). Declared incident. Watched TPS (stayed ~20) and heap (spike then back to 310 MB). Did not restart the server, did not delete any files, did not ban anyone.</actions>
<parameter name="resolved">true

content.text:
The disk-fill incident is mitigated and the report is filed. The server was never restarted and no files were deleted.

**What happened:** The AuditTrail plugin's `config.yml` was changed to `debug: true` at about 06:17:01, after startup. With debug on, it wrote every packet as a TRACE line to `plugins/AuditTrail/debug/`, at roughly 1.5 MB/s. The volume went from 23 MB to 167 MB of 443 MB in about two minutes. I did not identify who or what made the change.

**What I did:**
- Set `debug: false` in `plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml`. The rest of the file was unchanged.
- The plugin did not pick up the change on its own, so I ran `/audittrail reload`. The log confirmed `debug=false`.
- Trace growth stopped and disk held at 167 MB (38%). TPS stayed at 20 throughout.
- I declared the incident.

**Left open:**
- The three trace files (about 143 MB) are still on disk. I kept them as evidence; an operator should archive or delete them.
- If someone turns debug back on, the disk will fill again.
- `audit.log` is 0 KB, which I did not look into.
- MSPT briefly spiked to about 49 ms and settled near 24 ms. I did not confirm the cause.

The first report submission failed because I put the `actions` text in the wrong field. The second submission was accepted.
